name: Euler’s bridge traversal analysis
description: Euler analyzed whether all bridges in a network can be traversed once in a single walk, a foundation for later graph theory.

impact.note: One solved puzzle known to mathematicians, a modest result in itself, from which graph theory is conventionally traced.

date.basis: Hopkins and Wilson date Euler’s presentation to 26 August 1735; the written-paper dating differs between sources.

events.statement: Euler presented a general analysis of the Königsberg bridge problem in 1735; the paper appeared in print in 1741.

evidence.supports: The Euler Archive dates the bridge paper to 1735 writing and 1741 publication.
Hopkins and Wilson date presentation to 1735, write-up to 1736 and publication to 1741; the Euler Archive lists writing in 1735.

contributions.resource: Presented the general bridge traversal analysis.

evidence.supports: The Euler Archive dates the bridge paper to 1735 writing and 1741 publication.

earliest_record.rationale: Dated witness within the inspected evidence; not a global-priority claim.

caveats: The Euler Archive lists 1735 as the paper’s writing date; Hopkins and Wilson place presentation in 1735 and the write-up in 1736. Publication occurred in 1741. Euler did not use the full language of modern graph theory.
